title: Best GoHighLevel Alternative for Med Spas (October 2026)
summary: A GoHighLevel alternative for med spas should hold charts, bookings and leads in one record. Here is what to compare before you switch.
body_markdown:
## What GoHighLevel Does Well for a Med Spa


GoHighLevel is good at the top of the funnel: capturing a lead, texting it back, running a sequence and moving a contact through a pipeline. It was built for marketing agencies that run many client accounts, which is why so many med spas first meet it through an agency rather than buying it themselves.


That origin explains both the strengths and the friction. You get funnels, forms, a pipeline board, two-way texting and automation builders without a developer. A clinic with one location and one person watching the inbox gets less from the agency features and pays attention to the setup time instead. Owners we talk to rarely say the tool is bad. They say it is one more place to keep up to date.


## Where GoHighLevel Stops for a Clinic


GoHighLevel stops at the chart. Its pricing page describes contacts, sub-accounts, automation, calling and messaging, and says nothing about treatment notes, consent forms, injectable units or before-and-after photos. Everything clinical lives in another system.


Three gaps show up in clinics again and again.


- **No clinical record.** A lead becomes a patient in your EMR, and the CRM keeps the old lead. Someone has to link them, or the same person is counted twice.
- **Revenue lives somewhere else.** The CRM knows a lead booked. It does not know that the appointment was a $450 toxin visit or a $3,000 package unless you build the bridge. We cover that gap in[our guide to tracking Google and Meta leads to booked revenue](https://decodahealth.com/blog/google-meta-ads-lead-tracking-practice) .
- **Compliance is an add-on.** HIPAA coverage costs extra, and the agreement has to be signed before patient information goes in. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services explains[what a Business Associate Agreement must contain](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/covered-entities/sample-business-associate-agreement-provisions/index.html) , and it is worth reading before you sign one with any vendor.


## What GoHighLevel Costs a Single-Location Clinic


GoHighLevel lists three self-serve plans: Starter at $97 per month, Unlimited at $297 and Founder at $497, with Enterprise priced on request. Email, SMS and calling are usage-based on top of that, and the page does not publish per-message rates.


For one location, Starter covers the basics, but the HIPAA add-on at $297 per month more than triples the base price. Add the usage charges, and the practical cost depends on how many texts your sequences send. If you are comparing this to an all-in-one platform, price the whole stack, not one line. Our[clinic software cost breakdown](https://decodahealth.com/blog/clinic-software-cost-breakdown) walks through the tools a typical practice pays for at once.

## GoHighLevel Alternative for Med Spas: Three Ways to Handle the Gap


Clinics settle on one of three arrangements, and the right one depends on who runs your marketing today. Keeping both tools works when an agency manages the CRM and you have no wish to learn it. Merging into one platform works when the front desk is small and every extra login costs real time. Dropping the CRM works only when you do not run paid ads at all.


Here is how the first two compare in practice.


- **Keep GoHighLevel, add an EMR.** Lowest disruption. You carry two patient lists, two sets of automations and two bills. Reports on cost per booked patient need a manual join.
- **Move everything into one platform.** One patient record, one inbox and one set of reports. The work is the migration, and the risk is that the new tool's marketing features are thinner than a dedicated CRM. Check that before you commit.


Our[system of record guide](https://decodahealth.com/blog/system-of-record) explains why the second option tends to win as a clinic adds tools.


## Who Owns the Account Your Leads Land In


If an ad agency runs your GoHighLevel, ask who owns the account before anything else. Several owners we have spoken with run their entire lead flow, and sometimes their notes, inside an agency's own sub-account. When the contract ends, the contacts, conversation history and automations are the agency's to export or not.


Put three things in writing before you renew or leave: a full export of contacts and conversations on request, a named person who owns the ad accounts and the pixel, and the date the phone number porting request will be filed. An owner who skips this ends up rebuilding lead history from memory.


An agency can still run your ads after you move. Some owners ask whether they can give an agency limited access to marketing data without exposing patient records. Put that question to any vendor you evaluate, because the answer differs by platform.


## Six Questions to Ask Any GoHighLevel Alternative


These questions separate a platform that replaces the CRM from one that just resembles it. Ask them in the demo, and ask to see each answer on screen.


1. **Can I build an audience from treatment history?** For example, patients treated with toxin 90 days ago who have not rebooked. If the answer is an export, it is not integrated.
2. **Does a lead turn into a patient record without re-entry?** The pipeline stage should link to the chart. Our[AI lead routing guide](https://decodahealth.com/blog/ai-lead-routing-stop-losing-med-spa-leads) covers what should happen in the first minutes.
3. **Do Instagram DMs and texts land in one inbox?** A prospect asked this directly on a call, because their leads arrive on social as often as by form.
4. **Can I see cost per booked patient, not cost per lead?** Cost per lead is easy to get from any ad platform. Booked revenue is the number that decides spend.
5. **Who signs the Business Associate Agreement, and what does it cover?** Ask for it up front, as the HHS page above describes.
6. **What happens to my automations and phone number on the way in?** Ask for a written plan, not a promise.


## How Texting Rules Change the Switch


Moving platforms does not reset patient consent. Opt-ins and opt-outs travel with the contact, so carry the consent record across, not only the phone number. A patient who texted STOP to the old system must stay opted out in the new one.


The same applies to quiet hours and consent wording. Our guide to[med spa text message consent](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-text-message-consent) sets out what to record and how long to keep it, and it is the checklist to run before you import any contact list.


## GoHighLevel vs an EMR: What Clinics Run Side by Side


GoHighLevel and an EMR do different jobs, and most clinics that evaluate a switch are running both plus more. On sales calls this month, owners described stacks such as an EMR, GoHighLevel, a Google Voice number and an answering service, or an EMR with a separate email tool, a desk-phone line and QuickBooks.


Each added tool carries its own login, its own patient list and its own bill. The hidden cost shows up at month end. Revenue gets re-keyed by hand, lead sources get guessed, and nobody can say which campaign produced the patients who actually paid. A single clinic that adds a second service line, such as hormones or weight loss next to aesthetics, usually adds a tool at the same time.


Before you price a replacement, list every tool that touches a patient and what each one stores. If the same phone number appears in three of them, you have found the cost.


## What Moving Off GoHighLevel Takes


The export is the easy part. Contacts, tags and conversation history come out as files in an afternoon. The slow work is rebuilding the parts of the setup that actually earn money: the new-lead text, the consult reminder, the toxin recall and the review request.


List those four first and rebuild only those. Many clinics find that some of their old automations had stopped doing anything useful. ## Final Thoughts on Replacing GoHighLevel in a Med Spa


Decide by asking what you would lose if the CRM disappeared tomorrow. If the answer is only the follow-up texts, rebuild them in the system that already holds the chart. If the answer includes lead history you cannot export, fix ownership first and migrate second. Either way, price the whole stack, including the HIPAA add-on and usage charges, before you compare it with one platform.

## Frequently Asked Questions


Is GoHighLevel HIPAA compliant for a med spa?


Only if HIPAA coverage is switched on and a Business Associate Agreement is signed. GoHighLevel's pricing page says HIPAA compliance is included on its Enterprise plan and sold as a $297 per month add-on on the other plans. A med spa that stores treatment history, photos or health answers in any CRM should have the signed agreement in hand before the first record goes in.


Can GoHighLevel replace my med spa EMR?


No, not on its own. GoHighLevel is built around contacts, pipelines, funnels and messaging, and its pricing page does not describe charting, consent forms, injectable inventory or clinical notes. Most med spas that use it keep a separate EMR for the chart, which means every patient lives in two systems that someone has to keep matching by hand.


What should a med spa look for in a GoHighLevel alternative?


Look for one patient record that the chart, the calendar, the checkout and the marketing all read from. The test is simple. Can you build a text campaign for patients who had a toxin treatment 90 days ago without exporting a list? Decoda Health builds campaign audiences from the same records the clinic runs on, so that question has a one-step answer.


Can I keep GoHighLevel and add an EMR instead of switching?


You can, and many clinics do while they use an agency that already runs the account. The cost is a second source of truth. Lead status, appointment history and revenue sit in different places, so reporting on cost per booked patient means joining two exports. If you plan to end the agency contract, move the contacts out first and decide where lead history will live afterward.


How long does it take to move off GoHighLevel to another platform?


The contact export itself takes an afternoon. The slower part is rebuilding what hung off it: forms, automations, sequences and phone numbers. Decoda Health runs the entire migration itself and finishes in 3-4 weeks, guaranteed.
